title: Electrical Energy
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Integrated Science; not yet checked by a CBC Integrated Science teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Cells, a bulb holder, wires and a switch only (low voltage, never mains). The child builds a series circuit, removes one bulb, then builds a parallel circuit and does the same. Kenyan sources (Olkaria geothermal, Seven Forks hydro, Lake Turkana wind, solar panels on homes) are shown on a map.

skills.key_step: The child names sources of electricity (cells and batteries, solar panels, hydroelectric, geothermal, wind, generators) with Kenyan examples, and knows sockets and wires carry electricity but do not make it.

floor.prerequisite: Knows ways of lighting a house.
floor.question: Name one way of lighting a house at night.
floor.answer: electric bulbs or a solar lamp

representations: a map of Kenyan power stations
a cell, a small solar panel and a bulb
a chart: source, how it works, example
steps: Cells and batteries: chemical energy.
Solar panels: sunlight.
Hydro: falling water (Seven Forks); geothermal: underground heat (Olkaria).
Wind (Lake Turkana) and generators.
contexts: a solar panel on a homestead roof

board.do: Draw a dam, a steam well and a wind turbine.
Point at the steam well.
board.say: Which source is this, and where in Kenya?

board.do: Wait for "geothermal, Olkaria".
Label each source.

misconceptions.ask: Where does the electricity come from before the socket?
misconceptions.repair: Sockets and wires carry electricity from a source.

listen_for: it is stored in the wires
misconceptions.ask: What happens to the bulb when the source is switched off?
misconceptions.repair: Wires carry electricity; they do not store it.

misconceptions.ask: Which uses heat from under the ground?
misconceptions.repair: Hydro uses falling water; geothermal uses underground heat.

misconceptions.ask: What happened when the panel was covered?
misconceptions.repair: Solar panels work only in daylight.

checks.question: Name a source of electricity found in Kenya.
checks.answer: geothermal at Olkaria, hydro at Seven Forks, wind at Lake Turkana, or solar

checks.question: Is a socket a source of electricity?
checks.answer: No: it carries electricity from a source

skills.key_step: The child names the parts of a simple circuit (cell, wires, bulb, switch) and says the bulb lights only when there is a complete loop from one end of the cell back to the other.

floor.question: Is a bulb a source of light?

representations: a cell, two wires, a bulb and a switch
a drawing of a broken loop
steps: Join a wire from the + end to the bulb.
Join a wire from the bulb back to the - end.
The loop is complete: the bulb lights.
Open the switch: the loop is broken.

board.do: Draw a cell, a bulb and one wire joining them.
Ask whether the bulb will light.
Wait for the child's prediction.
Draw the second wire to the other end and write "complete circuit".

misconceptions.ask: Is there a way back to the cell?
misconceptions.repair: A circuit needs a complete loop.

listen_for: the bulb uses up the current
misconceptions.ask: Is the current the same on both sides of the bulb?
misconceptions.repair: The current is not used up; energy is.

listen_for: an open switch lets it through
misconceptions.ask: Is there a gap when the switch is open?
misconceptions.repair: An open switch breaks the circuit.

misconceptions.ask: Did the bulb light with both wires on +?
misconceptions.repair: One wire to each end of the cell.

checks.question: Why does a bulb not light if a wire is loose?
What does a switch do in a circuit?

skills.key_step: The child tells a series circuit (one loop; remove a bulb and all go out; bulbs dimmer) from a parallel circuit (separate branches; remove one and the rest stay on; bulbs as bright as one alone), and says houses are wired in parallel.

floor.question: What happens to a bulb if the switch is open?

representations: two-bulb series and parallel circuits built
steps: Series: one path through both bulbs.
Remove one bulb: the path breaks, all go out.
Parallel: each bulb has its own branch.
Remove one bulb: the others stay on.
contexts: old Christmas lights going out together

board.do: Draw a series circuit with two bulbs.
Ask what happens if one bulb is removed.
Wait for the child's prediction.
Cross out both bulbs and write "series: all go out".
Draw the parallel circuit beside it.

misconceptions.ask: Is there still a complete loop?
misconceptions.repair: In series, removing one bulb breaks the circuit.

misconceptions.ask: Which circuit had the brighter bulbs?
misconceptions.repair: Parallel bulbs are brighter than series ones.

misconceptions.ask: Do all the lights go off when one bulb blows at home?
misconceptions.repair: Houses are wired in parallel.

misconceptions.ask: What happened when a second bulb was added in series?
misconceptions.repair: In series, more bulbs means dimmer bulbs.

checks.question: In which circuit do the other bulbs stay on when one is removed?
Why are houses wired in parallel?
checks.answer: each light can be switched on and off on its own, and one blown bulb does not put out the rest

skills.key_step: The child names common electrical appliances and the useful energy each gives: bulb (light), iron, kettle and cooker (heat), radio and speaker (sound), fan and blender (movement), television (light and sound).

floor.prerequisite: Knows heat and sound are forms of energy.
floor.question: What is the source of sound in a drum?

representations: a fan and a radio switched on (teacher)
steps: Name the appliance.
Ask: what does it give that we use?
Light, heat, sound or movement.
Some give more than one.

board.do: Draw a kettle, a radio and a fan.
Point at the fan.
board.say: What useful energy does it give?

board.do: Wait for "movement (kinetic)".
Ask the child to label the others.

misconceptions.ask: What happens to the radio when unplugged?
misconceptions.repair: Appliances use electricity; they do not make it.

misconceptions.ask: What do you hear from a radio?
misconceptions.repair: A radio changes electricity into sound.

misconceptions.ask: Why is the back of a fridge warm?
misconceptions.repair: A fridge moves heat out from inside.

misconceptions.ask: What do you feel from an iron?
misconceptions.repair: An iron gives mainly heat.

checks.question: What useful energy does an electric kettle give?
Name an appliance that changes electricity into sound.
checks.answer: a radio, a speaker or a television

skills.key_step: The child chooses safe ways of using electricity: dry hands, pull the plug not the cable, do not overload sockets, keep water away, never touch broken wires or play near power lines, and call an adult or KPLC.

floor.prerequisite: Can name appliances and the energy they give.
floor.question: What energy does an iron give?

representations: a picture of a home with dangers
steps: Dry hands and keep water away.
Pull the plug, not the cable.
One appliance per socket; do not overload.
Stay away from broken wires and power lines; tell an adult.
contexts: a broken power line after a storm

board.do: Draw a socket with five plugs in an adaptor.
Point at the adaptor.
Wait for "overheating, fire".
Ask the child to draw the safe way.

misconceptions.ask: Does water carry electricity?
misconceptions.repair: Never touch switches with wet hands.

misconceptions.ask: What can happen to the wires inside?
misconceptions.repair: Hold the plug to pull it out; leave repairs to an electrician.

misconceptions.ask: What happens to the wires with too many plugs?
misconceptions.repair: Overloading can cause a fire.

listen_for: it is fine if it does not touch
misconceptions.ask: What if the string blows onto the wire?
misconceptions.repair: Never play near power lines.

checks.question: Why should you never touch a switch with wet hands?
checks.answer: water conducts electricity and you could get a shock

checks.question: What should you do if you see a fallen power line?
checks.answer: keep away and tell an adult or KPLC
